extraction_notes: Vegetable tanning extract from quebracho (Schinopsis) heartwood. Heading 3201 specific.
Wattle/mimosa bark extract — Acacia mearnsii tannin, dominant Indian/South African tanning source.
Gambier (Uncaria gambir) leaf extract — Indonesian/Malaysian astringent tannin source. India-specific 8-digit split under 3201.90.
Myrobalan (Terminalia chebula) fruit extract — major Indian tanning source, also used in inks/dyeing.
Gallotannic acid / digallic acid — purified tannin (still under 3201 because of HS Note: tannic acid extracted from vegetable origin remains here, not 2918).
Other vegetable tanning extracts not covered above (e.g., chestnut, oak, sumac, valonia).
Syntans — sulphonated naphthalene/phenol formaldehyde condensates used as auxiliary or replacement tanning agents.

Inorganic tanning materials — basic chromium sulphate (dominant), alum, zirconium salts. Numeric metal pcts not populated (Ch.32 grouping treats these as preparations, not tariff-distinguishing assays).
Compounded tanning preparations — formulations possibly combining vegetable tannins, syntans, and auxiliaries.
Bating enzymes (proteases) used in pre-tanning to soften pelts. Borderline with 3507 (enzymes) but classified here when put up as tanning preparation per HS Note.
Residual catch-all under 3202.90 — other inorganic tanning substances/preparations not specified above.
Cutch/catechu — Acacia catechu extract. Despite being a tannin, India places it under 3203 (colouring matter) because of dye/khaki use; 8-digit India-specific.
Non-synthetic natural food colours (e.g., turmeric, paprika extract, beetroot red, annatto). Excludes synthetic food colours (those fall under 3204.19.8x).
Lac-dye — extracted from lac insect (Kerria lacca) secretion. India-specific given the country's traditional lac industry.
Natural indigo from Indigofera tinctoria — distinguished from synthetic indigo (CI Vat Blue 1 at 3204.15.51). India's heritage natural dye.
Other natural colouring matter — henna, madder, logwood, cochineal, etc.
CI Disperse Yellow 13 (Duranol Brill Yellow 6G). Disperse dyes are non-ionic, water-insoluble — used for hydrophobic fibres (polyester, acetate).
Other disperse yellows not specifically listed (e.g., CI Disperse Yellow 3, 23, 42, 54).
CI Disperse Orange 11 (Duranol Orange G) — anthraquinone-type orange disperse dye.
Other disperse oranges (e.g., CI Disperse Orange 1, 3, 25, 30, 37).
CI Disperse Red 3 (Serisol Fast Pink B) — azo disperse pink/red.
CI Disperse Red 4 (Celliton Fast Pink RF) — anthraquinone pink for cellulose acetate.
CI Disperse Red 9 (Duranol Red GN) — methylaminoanthraquinone red.
Other disperse reds not specifically listed (e.g., CI Disperse Red 1, 11, 13, 17, 60).
CI Disperse Violet 1 (Duranol Violet 2R) — 1,4-diaminoanthraquinone, classic anthraquinone violet.
CI Disperse Violet 4 (Duranol Brill Violet B) — anthraquinone violet, brilliant shade.
CI Disperse Violet 8 (Duranol Brill Violet BR) — anthraquinone violet variant.
Other disperse violets — residual after 1/4/8.
CI Disperse Blue 1 (Duranol Brill Blue CB) — 1,4,5,8-tetraamino anthraquinone, hair dye + textile.
CI Disperse Blue 3 (Duranol Brill Blue BBN) — anthraquinone blue.
CI Disperse Blue 5 (Celliton Fast Blue FFB) — anthraquinone, originally for cellulose acetate.
CI Disperse Blue 6 (Celliton Fast Blue FFG) — anthraquinone blue.
CI Disperse Blue 14 (Duranol Brill Blue G) — 1,4-bis(methylamino)anthraquinone.
CI Disperse Blue 24 (Duranol Blue 2G) — anthraquinone blue, greenish shade.
Other disperse blues (e.g., Blue 7, 26, 56, 60, 73, 79, 165) not specifically listed.
Disperse greens — typically anthraquinone-based or blue/yellow mixtures.
Disperse browns — single-component browns (Disperse Brown 1, 19 etc.).
Disperse blacks — single component blacks (Disperse Black 1, 9).
Disperse brown blends — formulated brown mixtures from multiple chromophores.
Disperse grey blends — formulated mixtures yielding greys for polyester.
Disperse black blends — typical trichromy blends (red+blue+yellow) producing black shades on PET.
Catch-all under 3204.11.99 — other disperse dyes not falling into colour categories above.
Azo acid yellows — sulphonated azo dyes for protein/polyamide fibres in acid bath.
Azo acid oranges (e.g., Acid Orange 7, 10, 12) — sulphonated monoazo or disazo.
Azo acid reds — heavily exported subgroup (Acid Red 18 ponceau 4R, Acid Red 27 amaranth, Acid Red 88).
Azo acid violets — generally disazo with bridging amino groups.
Azo acid blues — e.g., metal-complex 1:2 chrome blues.
Azo acid greens (rare; most acid greens are triphenylmethane in the non-azo subcategory).
Azo acid browns — typically polyazo metallised browns (large for wool/leather).
Azo acid blacks — e.g., Acid Black 1, 24, 26 — disazo or trisazo black workhorses.
Other azo acid dyes not falling into the named colour groups.
CI Acid Green 17 (Solacet Fast Green 2G) — triphenylmethane sulphonate.
CI Acid Green 27 (Carbolan Green G) — milling-class anthraquinone wool dye.
CI Acid Green 28 (Carbolan Brill Green 5G) — anthraquinone milling green, brilliant shade.
CI Acid Green 38 (Alizarine Cyanine Green 3G) — alizarine derivative.
CI Acid Green 44 (Alizarine Cyanine Green GWA) — alizarine-cyanine class, fastness-rated for wool.
Other non-azo acid greens not specifically itemised.
CI Acid Black 2 (nigrosine, water-soluble form) — phenazine-derived black, widely used in leather finishing.
CI Acid Black 48 (Coomassie Fast Grey 3G) — anthraquinone non-azo black/grey.
Other non-azo acid blacks.
CI Acid Blue 2 (Alizarine Brill Blue PFN) — alizarine-class anthraquinone blue.
CI Acid Blue 14 (Solacet Fast Blue 4G) — non-azo, often anthraquinone-sulphonate.
CI Acid Blue 23 (Alizarine Light Blue 4G).
CI Acid Blue 25 (Solway Ultra Blue B) — leveling-class anthraquinone, very common.
CI Acid Blue 45 (Solway Blue RN) — anthraquinone with histology use.
CI Acid Blue 51 (Alizarine Sky Blue FFB) — alizarine-derivative sky blue.
CI Acid Blue 52 (Alizarine Light 5GL) — light shade alizarine derivative.
CI Acid Blue 78 (Solway Sky Blue B) — anthraquinone sky blue.
CI Acid Blue 93 (Ink Blue) — water-soluble methyl-violet derivative, used for inks.
CI Acid Blue 112 (Coomassie Ultra Sky SE) — sulphonated diphenyl-methane derivative.
CI Acid Blue 127 (Brill Alizarine Milling Blue G) — anthraquinone milling blue.
CI Acid Blue 138 (Carbolan Blue B) — milling-class anthraquinone for wool.
CI Acid Blue 140 (Carbolan Brill Blue 2R) — brilliant milling blue.
Other non-azo acid blues outside the listed CI-numbered set.
Mordant yellows — chromable dyes requiring metallic mordant (typically chromium) to develop.
Mordant oranges — chromable orange dyes.
Mordant violets — e.g., Mordant Violet 5, 28.
Mordant blues — Mordant Blue 1, 13, 29 (eriochrome blue).
Mordant greens — uncommon class, mostly metal complexed phthalein derivatives.
Mordant browns — Mordant Brown 1, 33 — chrome-developed browns.
Mordant blacks — Mordant Black 11 (Eriochrome Black T, also a complexometric indicator), 17.
Mordant Red 2 a.k.a. alizarine red — original synthetic dye replacing madder. Description text reads 'Red II' (Roman numeral).
Other mordant dyes outside the named colour groups.
Other non-azo acid yellows — typically pyrazolone, quinoline, nitro yellows.
Other non-azo acid oranges — quinophthalone / anthraquinone oranges.
Other non-azo acid reds — typically anthraquinone or xanthene (e.g., Acid Red 52 = sulphorhodamine).
Other non-azo acid violets — anthraquinone (e.g., Acid Violet 43) and triphenylmethane.
Other non-azo acid browns — relatively few, mostly metallised brown complexes.
Catch-all under 3204.12.99 — other non-azo acid dyes not in a named subgroup.
Basic azo dyes (cationic) — bind acid-modified acrylic. Examples: Basic Yellow 11, Basic Red 14.
CI Basic Yellow 2 (Auramine O) — diphenylmethane cationic. Also used as Ziehl-Neelsen mycobacterial stain.
Other basic yellows (non-azo) — typically methine or thiazole types.
CI Basic Red 1 (Rhodamine 6G) — fluorescent xanthene dye, also a laser dye.
Other non-azo basic reds — xanthene/oxazine fluorescent reds.
CI Basic Violet 1 (Methyl Violet 2B) — triphenylmethane violet, key ink colorant.
CI Basic Violet 10 (Rhodamine B) — xanthene fluorescent reddish-violet, tracer dye.
CI Basic Violet 14 (Magenta / Basic Fuchsine) — triphenylmethane, classic magenta dye.
Other non-azo basic violets — Basic Violet 3 (crystal violet, gentian violet).
CI Basic Blue 9 (Methylene Blue) — phenothiazine derivative. Also indicator and pharmaceutical (methaemoglobinaemia treatment).
CI Basic Blue 16 (Victoria Blue B) — naphthotriphenylmethane.
Other non-azo basic blues — Basic Blue 26, 41, 54 (acrylic dyeing).
CI Basic Green 4 (Malachite Green) — triphenylmethane. Banned in food fish (Indian seafood regulation).
Other non-azo basic greens — Basic Green 1 (brilliant green).
Non-azo basic oranges — e.g., chrysoidine substitutes.
Non-azo basic browns — leather and paper applications.
Non-azo basic blacks — induline, nigrosine-related (water-soluble basic forms).
Catch-all for non-azo basic dyes outside the named colour categories.
CI Direct Yellow 12 (Chrysophenine G) — stilbene-type direct yellow. (Note: input header text appears mislabelled 'non-azo basic' but heading 3204.14 is direct dyes.)
Other direct yellows — typically polyazo or stilbene-based substantive dyes for cotton.
Congo Red (CI Direct Red 28) — first synthetic direct dye for cotton; benzidine-derived, now restricted in EU/India for textile use.
Other azo direct reds — Direct Red 23, 81 (post-benzidine alternatives).
CI Direct Blue 1 (Sky Blue FF) — disazo direct dye from benzidine series.
Other azo direct blues — Direct Blue 71, 86 (copper phthalocyanine variant).
Azo direct oranges (e.g., Direct Orange 26, 39).
Azo direct greens — polyazo greens for cotton.
Azo direct browns — Direct Brown 95, 154 (high tonnage for cotton/jute).
Azo direct blacks — Direct Black 22, 38, 168 (post-benzidine).
Non-azo direct yellows — stilbene-based (Direct Yellow 11 etc.).
Non-azo direct oranges — relatively uncommon class.
Non-azo direct reds — uncommon outside specialty applications.
Non-azo direct violets — sirius / chlorazol violet variants.
Non-azo direct blues — copper phthalocyanine direct blues (Direct Blue 86 etc.).
Non-azo direct greens — Cu-phthalocyanine green direct variants (rare).
Non-azo direct browns — uncommon variants.
Non-azo direct blacks — relatively uncommon, special-purpose.
Other non-azo direct dyes (within 3204.14.89 catch-all).
Final residual under 3204.14 — other direct dyes not in subgroups above.
CI Vat Yellow 2 (GC) — thioindigoid yellow vat dye.
CI Vat Yellow 4 (Indanthrene Golden Yellow GK) — dibenzpyrenequinone golden yellow.
Other vat yellows — Vat Yellow 1, 12, 33.
CI Vat Orange 3 (Brilliant Orange RK) — perylene vat orange.
CI Vat Orange 15 (Golden Orange 3G) — dibenzanthrone orange.
Other vat oranges (e.g., Vat Orange 1, 7, 9).
Vat Red (Brilliant Pink) — anthrapyrimidine pink vat dye.
Other vat reds — Vat Red 13, 14, 15.
CI Vat Violet 1 (Brilliant Violet 2R) — dibenzanthrone-derived violet.
CI Vat Violet 3 (Magenta B) — thioindigoid violet.
Other vat violets — Vat Violet 9, 13, 15.
Synthetic indigo (CI Vat Blue 1, indigotin) — the workhorse dye for denim, contrasted with natural indigo at 3203.00.40.
CI Vat Blue 4 (Indanthrone) — the original anthraquinone vat blue, used as pigment too.
CI Vat Blue 5 (Blue 2B) — dichlorinated indanthrone derivative.
CI Vat Blue 6 (Blue BC) — anthraquinone vat blue.
CI Vat Blue 20 (Dark Blue 30) — dibenzopyrenequinone dark blue.
CI Vat Blue 29 (Indanthrene Brill Blue 4G) — brilliant blue anthraquinone.
CI Vat Blue 43 (Carbazole Blue) — heterocyclic carbazole-based vat dye.
Pre-reduced vat blue (leuco-form) — supplied ready-reduced for continuous dyeing of cotton/denim.
Other vat blues not in the listed CI numbers (e.g., Vat Blue 14, 16, 35, 64).
CI Vat Green 1 (Indanthrene Brilliant Green BFFB) — the most important vat green, dimethoxy-dibenzanthrone.
CI Vat Green 2 (Indanthrene Brilliant Green GG) — yellower-shade variant.
CI Vat Green 4 (Indanthrene Brilliant Green 3B) — bluer-shade green vat dye.
CI Vat Green 9 (Black BB) — anthraquinone dark green / olive-black.
Other vat greens — Vat Green 3, 11, 13.
CI Vat Brown 1 (Brown BR) — anthraquinone vat brown.
CI Vat Brown 3 (Brown RGR) — reddish-brown anthraquinone vat.
CI Vat Brown 5 (Brown RRD, G) — anthraquinone brown variant.
Other vat browns — Vat Brown 25, 39, 44.
CI Vat Black 9 (Black RB) — anthraquinone vat black.
CI Vat Black 25 (Olive T) — olive-black anthraquinone shade.
CI Vat Black 27 (Olive R) — anthraquinone olive variant.
CI Vat Black 29 (Grey BG) — anthraquinone grey-black.
Other vat blacks — Vat Black 8, 13, 22.
Solubilised vat yellows (Indigosol-type sulphate-ester leucos) — yellow shades.
Solubilised vat oranges (Indigosols).
Solubilised vat reds.
Solubilised vat violets.
Solubilised vat blues (Indigosol Blue).
Solubilised vat greens.
Solubilised vat blacks.
Final catch-all under 3204.15 vat dyes — other vat/solubilised-vat preparations not specifically classified.
Reactive yellows — monoazo or formazan with reactive anchor (dichlorotriazine/vinylsulphone) for covalent bonding to cellulose.
Reactive oranges — monoazo reactives for cotton (e.g., Reactive Orange 13, 16).
Reactive reds — large class. Reactive Red 120, 195, 198 widely exported by Indian dye makers (Gujarat).
Reactive violets — Reactive Violet 5 (vinylsulphone) etc.
Reactive blues — Reactive Blue 19, 21 (turquoise = Cu-phthalocyanine), 220.
Reactive greens — Reactive Green 12, 19 (phthalocyanine-based).
Reactive browns — Reactive Brown 10, 11, 17, 23, 33.
Reactive blacks — Reactive Black 5 (a top-3 reactive dye globally, double vinylsulphone).
Other reactive dyes / blends not in colour buckets above.
CI Pigment Yellow 1 (Hansa Yellow G) — monoazo organic pigment for paints/inks.
Other pigment yellows (Pigment Yellow 3, 12 diarylide, 14, 17, 74, 83, 138 isoindolinone, 151 benzimidazolone).
Pigment oranges (PO 5 dinitraniline, 13, 16, 34, 36, 43, 64, 73 — wide spread of azo/dpp/benzimidazolone classes).
Toluidine Red (CI Pigment Red 3) — monoazo red pigment, classic ink/paint red.
Other pigment reds (PR 48 Ba/Ca/Mn lake, 53:1, 57:1 Litho rubine, 81 PTMA, 122 quinacridone, 146, 254 DPP, 268).
Pigment violets — PV 19 quinacridone, PV 23 carbazole violet, PV 27 PTMA.
CI Pigment Blue 15 (copper phthalocyanine) — the workhorse blue organic pigment; many crystal modifications (15:1, 15:3, 15:4, 15:6) span this code.
Other pigment blues (PB 1 alkali blue, 16 metal-free phthalocyanine, 60 indanthrone).
CI Pigment Green 7 (chlorinated copper phthalocyanine) — workhorse green organic pigment. Description misspelled 'Pathalovyanine' in source.
Other pigment greens — PG 36 (chlorobromo-phthalocyanine, yellower green).
Pigment browns — PBr 23 disazo condensation, 24 chromium titanate, 25 benzimidazolone.
Pigment blacks — PBk 1 aniline black, 31 perylene black, 32 perylene. (Carbon black is in Ch.28.)
Catch-all for other organic pigments / preparations based thereon.
New 2017 HS subheading isolating carotenoids (beta-carotene, lutein, lycopene, astaxanthin, canthaxanthin) and their preparations.
Azoic Coupling Component 2 (Naphthol AS) — the parent naphtholAS, 3-hydroxy-2-naphthoyl-anilide; key coupling component for ice-dyeing cotton.
Azoic Coupling Component 4 (Naphthol AS-BO) — methoxy-substituted variant.
Azoic Coupling Component 5 (Naphthol ASG) — acetoacetic-aryl-amide green-coupling component.
Azoic Coupling Component 7 (Naphthol AS-SW).
Azoic Coupling Component 8 (Naphthol AS-TR).
Azoic Coupling Component 13 (Naphthol AS-SG).
Azoic Coupling Component 14 (Naphthol AS-PH).
Azoic Coupling Component 15 (Naphthol AS-LB).
Azoic Coupling Component 17 (Naphthol AS-BS).
Azoic Coupling Component 18 (Naphthol AS-D).
Azoic Coupling Component 20 (Naphthol AS-OL).
Other azoic coupling components — Naphthol AS series outside the listed numbers.
Azoic Diazo Component 1 (Fast Bordeaux GP Base) — diazotisable aromatic amine or stabilised diazonium salt. chemical_class=diazonium_salt applies (specific enum value).
Azoic Diazo Component 2 (Fast Orange G/GC Base) — o-nitroaniline base.
Azoic Diazo Component 3 (Fast Scarlet GG/GGS Base).
Azoic Diazo Component 4 (Fast Garnet GBC Base) — source description misspells 'Garment' as 'Garnet'.
Azoic Diazo Component 5 (Fast Red B Base) — 5-nitro-o-anisidine derivative.
Azoic Diazo Component 6 (Fast Orange GR Base) — m-nitro-o-anisidine.
Azoic Diazo Component 10 (Fast Red R Base) — m-nitro-p-toluidine.
Azoic Diazo Component 11 (Fast Red TR Base) — 4-chloro-o-toluidine.
Azoic Diazo Component 12 (Fast Scarlet G Base).
Azoic Diazo Component 13 (Fast Scarlet R Base).
Azoic Diazo Component 20 (Fast Blue BB Base) — Variamine Blue derivative.
Azoic Diazo Component 24 (Fast Blue RR Base).
Azoic Diazo Component 32 (Fast Red KB Base) — 5-chloro-2-aminotoluene derivative.
Azoic Diazo Component 41 (Fast Violet B Base).
Azoic Diazo Component 48 (Fast Blue B Base) — o-dianisidine-tetrazotised stabilised salt; restricted carcinogen in many regions.
Other azoic diazo components — Fast Yellow GC, Fast Black K Base, etc.
Azoic yellows — fully formed azoic colour (pre-coupled).
Azoic oranges — pre-coupled fast oranges.
Azoic reds — pre-formed.
Azoic violets — pre-formed.
Azoic blues — pre-formed.
Azoic greens — pre-formed.
Azoic browns — pre-formed.
Azoic blacks — pre-formed.
Other azoic colours not in named colour groups.
Sulphur yellows — sulphur dyes formed by thionation of aromatic amines/phenols.
Sulphur oranges — relatively limited subclass.
Sulphur reds — rare subclass.
Sulphur blues — Sulphur Blue 7, 9, 15 (also Indo Carbon, alternative to indigo for denim).
Sulphur greens — Sulphur Green 2, 3 (workwear/uniform applications).
Sulphur browns — Sulphur Brown 10, 51 — used for jute / cotton sacking.
Sulphur Black 1 — top tonnage sulphur dye worldwide, used on cotton (workwear, denim weft).
Other sulphur dyes — Leuco-sulphur stabilised forms (pre-reduced).
Solvent yellows — Solvent Yellow 14 (Sudan I — restricted), Solvent Yellow 33 (quinoline yellow base).
Solvent oranges — Solvent Orange 60, 62 (perinone), 86 (xanthene).
Solvent reds — Solvent Red 24, 26 (kerosene marker), 135, 179 (perinone). Indian fuel marking uses Solvent Red 164.
Solvent violets — Solvent Violet 13 (anthraquinone, plastic colorant).
Solvent blues — Solvent Blue 35 (oil-blue B for petroleum), Solvent Blue 36.
Solvent greens — Solvent Green 3 (anthraquinone), Solvent Green 7 (pyranine).
Solvent browns — Solvent Brown 1, 22 (azo).
Solvent blacks — Solvent Black 5, 7, 27, 29 (Cr-complex), 34.
Other solvent dyes — including fluorescent solvent dyes for plastics.
Food Yellow 3 (Sunset Yellow FCF, E110, INS 110) — sulphonated monoazo, FSSAI-permitted food colour.
Food Yellow 4 (Tartrazine, E102, INS 102) — pyrazolone azo. FSSAI-permitted.
Food Reds 5-8 (Ponceau family, includes Ponceau 4R / E124) — sulphonated azo reds.
Food Red 9 (Amaranth, E123, INS 123) — sulphonated azo bluish-red. Permitted in India, restricted in US.
Food oranges — currently no permitted FSSAI synthetic food orange; effectively a catch-all for legacy.
Food violets — historically Food Violet 2; not currently permitted in India.
Food greens — Fast Green FCF (CI Food Green 3, E143) — triphenylmethane, FSSAI-permitted.
Food browns — Brown HT (E155); not permitted in India.
Other synthetic food colours not specifically itemised (e.g., Erythrosine E127, Brilliant Blue FCF E133, Indigo Carmine E132).
Final catch-all under 3204.19 — synthetic organic colouring matter outside all named subgroups.
Optical brightening agents (OBAs / FWAs) — UV-absorbing fluorescent compounds. Typical: triazinyl-stilbene (Tinopal CBS-X, DBS-X) and coumarin/benzoxazole types.
Other synthetic organic products used as fluorescent brightening agents.
Other synthetic organic colouring matters (residual under 3204.90) — e.g., synthetic luminophores classed here per HS Note 5.
Colour lakes (Note 3) — soluble organic dyes precipitated onto an inorganic base (typically alumina). Includes FD&C aluminum lakes for tablet coating.
Pearlescent pigments — mica platelets coated with TiO2 (and/or iron oxide). Note: description misspells 'micaceous'. Code is in 3206.11 (TiO2 >=80%-coating) per India's 8-digit split.
Other TiO2-based pigments containing >=80% TiO2 by weight on dry basis (per subheading note). titanium_pct intentionally not populated (single-element grade not assayed at customs).
TiO2-based preparations containing <80% TiO2 (extended pigments, masterbatches).

Chromium-based pigments — chrome yellow (lead chromate, PY 34), chrome orange, chromium oxide green (Cr2O3, PG 17), molybdate orange. Lead-containing variants regulated under hazardous-chemical rules.
Ultramarine (CI Pigment Blue 29) — synthetic lapis-lazuli analogue. Also bluing for laundry.
Lithopone — co-precipitated ZnS/BaSO4 white pigment. Lower-cost alternative to TiO2.
Red iron oxide (PR 101) — synthetic or natural Fe2O3 red pigment. Workhorse construction/primer red.
Persian red — high-tinting-strength bluish-red iron oxide (colcothar / English red / Indian red).

Yellow ochre — natural earth pigment based on hydrated iron oxide (goethite, PY 43). Note: natural earth pigments not chemically calcined fall under 2530, but yellow ochre as a prepared pigment for paint sits here.
Bronze powder — fine Cu-Zn brass flakes for gold-effect paints/inks. (Distinct from aluminum paste at 3212.90.30 and metallic paint flakes at 3210.00.30.)
Other inorganic pigments — cobalt blue, manganese violet, Prussian blue, cadmium yellow/red.
Inorganic luminophores / phosphors — typical: ZnS:Cu (green glow), SrAl2O4:Eu/Dy (afterglow), Y2O3:Eu (red TV phosphor).
Prepared organic dye-stuff pigment in dry form — for ceramic/glass/enamel decoration (3207 scope per Note: pigments and similar preparations for ceramic, vitreous enamels, glass).
Prepared organic dye-stuff pigment in paste form — for direct application to ceramic.
Prepared inorganic pigments — ceramic stains (zirconium-praseodymium yellow, cobalt aluminate blue, ZrSiO4 base) ready for high-temp firing.
Prepared opacifiers / colours for ceramic enamels — typically based on ZrSiO4 or SnO2.
Other prepared pigments / colours / opacifiers for ceramic decoration not in named subgroups.
Vitrifiable enamels and glazes — used on ceramic tiles, sanitaryware, porcelain enamel cookware.
Engobes (slips) — clay/colorant suspensions for under-glaze decoration of tile / pottery.
Liquid lustres — solutions of gold/platinum/silver resinates in volatile solvents for decorative metallic films on glass/porcelain after firing.
Glass frit / cullet (powder / granule / flake form) — feed for enamels, glass-ceramic seals, electronic component packaging.
Polyester-based enamel in non-aqueous medium. 3208 covers paints/varnishes based on synthetic polymers in non-aqueous medium; subheading 3208.10 = polyester binder (in HS 2022).
Polyester-based lacquer in non-aqueous medium.
Polyester-based varnish (clear/unpigmented) in non-aqueous medium.
Other polyester-based paints/coatings (gel-coats, structural coatings) in non-aqueous medium.
Acrylic / vinyl polymer enamel in non-aqueous medium (3208.20 subheading).
Acrylic / vinyl polymer lacquer in non-aqueous medium.
Acrylic / vinyl polymer varnish in non-aqueous medium.
Other acrylic/vinyl-based coatings (e.g., adhesion primer) in non-aqueous medium.
Nitrocellulose (NC) lacquer — fast-drying solvent lacquer based on cellulose nitrate. Heavily used in Indian furniture and footwear finishing.
Other lacquers under 3208.90 — non-NC, non-acrylic types.
Alkyd synthetic enamel, ultra-white shade — the classic Indian solvent-borne 'enamel paint' for metal/wood (high TiO2 loading).
Alkyd synthetic enamel in coloured shades — non-white variants of the previous code.
Other synthetic enamels (non-alkyd) in non-aqueous medium.
Lacquers under 3208.90 (excluding NC at .11 and solvent-lacquers at .19).
Insulating varnish — dielectric coating for motor coils, transformer windings (Thermal Class B/F/H).
Other varnishes (non-insulating, non-polyester, non-acrylic) in non-aqueous medium.
Slip agents — fatty-amide-type lubricating additives in coatings; reduces surface friction.
Other paints/varnishes based on synthetic polymers in non-aqueous medium (final catch-all under 3208).
Acrylic emulsion paint — the dominant water-based decorative paint chemistry. 3209.10 covers acrylic/vinyl polymers in aqueous medium.
Other acrylic/vinyl water-based paints (non-emulsion variants).
Dispersion paints — water-borne paints where the polymer is dispersed (not necessarily acrylic).
Emulsion paints not elsewhere specified — non-acrylic water-based emulsions (e.g., styrene-butadiene, PVA emulsion).
Other water-based paints/varnishes based on synthetic polymers (residual under 3209.90).
Dry distemper / cement-based water paint — Indian low-cost wall coating, mixed with water at site.
Oil-bound distemper (OBD) — emulsion of drying oil in water suspension of chalk/pigment.
Other distempers not covered by .11/.12.
Prepared water pigments for leather finishing — top-coats, pad colours used by Indian leather industry.
Metallic powder/flake prepared as paint (silver/gold/bronze effect heat-resistant exhaust/radiator paint).
PTFE / silicone resin-based coating materials — non-stick cookware coatings (Teflon-type) and high-temperature silicone coatings.
Other paints / varnishes (incl. distempers, oil-paints, prepared water pigments for leather) not in named subgroups under 3210.
Prepared driers — metal-soap catalysts (cobalt, manganese, zirconium, lead, calcium octoates/naphthenates) that accelerate oxidative cure of alkyd paints.
Hot-stamping foils — multilayer carrier + release + metallic/pigment layer + adhesive, transferred by heat & pressure.
Pigments ground into linseed oil / white spirit / spirit of turpentine / varnish — colour pastes for tinting paints.
Dyes/colouring matter put up in retail packings (small sachets / bottles for household tie-dye, fabric refresh, holi-colour-like applications).
Aluminium paste — leafing/non-leafing flake suspended in solvent. Used for silver paints and printing inks.
Other pigment preparations / colouring matter dispersions under 3212.90.
Artists'/students' colours in sets — boxed assortments of water/oil/acrylic colours with brushes, palette etc.
Other artists'/students'/sign-writers' colours — individual tubes / tablets / bottles (not in sets).
Glaziers'/grafting putty, resin cements, caulking compounds, mastics, painters' fillings — broad sealants/fillers grouping.
Non-refractory surfacing preparations — wall putty, levelling compounds, texture finishes for facades/interiors. Distinct from refractory ceramics in Ch.38.
Resin cement — usually epoxy or polyester thermosetting cement for chemical-resistant flooring/anchoring.
Other sealants/putties/non-refractory surfacing preparations not classified above — silicone sealants, polyurethane sealants, butyl mastics.
Black lithographic / offset printing ink (3215.11 = black inks). 'Jelly' refers to high-viscosity offset-press ink form.
News ink (black) — coldset web offset ink for newsprint, fast absorption into uncoated newsprint.
Black rotary press ink — for letterpress/flexo/gravure rotary printing.
Black screen printing ink — for screen/silk-screen process on fabric/paper/plastic.
Other black printing inks not in named process subgroups.
Coloured lithographic / offset printing ink (3215.19 = other-than-black).
Coloured news ink — process colours for colour-newspaper printing.
Coloured rotary press inks (gravure/flexo).
Coloured screen printing ink — for fabric/paper/plastic screen printing.
Other coloured printing inks (final 3215.19 catch-all).
Fountain pen ink — dye-based aqueous ink (in solution).
Ball-pen ink — high-viscosity paste based on dyes in fatty-acid / glycol vehicle (oil-based or gel-pen formulations).
Indelible ink — the iconic Mysore Paints silver-nitrate-based election ink used to mark voters' fingernails in Indian elections.
Drawing ink (India ink) — fine carbon-black pigment in shellac/water binder. For drafting, calligraphy.
Other inks — inkjet cartridges, stamp-pad inks, marker inks, security inks (final catch-all under 3215).
